title: After 84 days in space, the last crew of the temporary American space station Skylab return to Earth.
text: Outer space, or simply space, is the expanse that exists beyond Earth's atmosphere and between celestial bodies. It contains ultra-low levels of particle densities, constituting a near-perfect vacuum of predominantly hydrogen and helium plasma, permeated by electromagnetic radiation, cosmic rays, neutrinos, magnetic fields and dust.

title: February 13–15 – Sagittarius A*, thought to be the location of a supermassive black hole, is identified by Bruce Balick and Robert Brown using the baseline interferometer of the United States National Radio Astronomy Observatory.
text: Sagittarius A*, abbreviated as Sgr A*, is the supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center of the Milky Way. Viewed from Earth, it is located near the border of the constellations Sagittarius and Scorpius, about 5.6° south of the ecliptic, visually close to the Butterfly Cluster (M6) and Lambda Scorpii.

title: Arecibo message transmitted from Arecibo Observatory (Puerto Rico) to Messier 13.
text: The Arecibo Observatory, also known as the National Astronomy and Ionosphere Center and formerly known as the Arecibo Ionosphere Observatory, is an observatory in Barrio Esperanza, Arecibo, Puerto Rico, owned by the US National Science Foundation (NSF). title: Hawking radiation is predicted by Stephen Hawking.
text: Stephen William Hawking was an English theoretical astrophysicist, cosmologist, and author who was director of research at the Centre for Theoretical Cosmology at the University of Cambridge. Between 1979 and 2009, he was the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge, widely viewed as one of the most prestigious academic posts in the world.

title: Novelist Juan Carlos Onetti is one of a group arrested by the Uruguayan dictatorship for selecting as a competition prizewinner and publishing in the newspaper Marcha a short story implicitly critical of the military regime. He…
text: A novelist is an author or writer of novels. Novelists can also write in other genres of both fiction and non-fiction.

title: After publication at the end of 1973 of Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn's The Gulag Archipelago (Russian: Архипелаг ГУЛАГ), the author is arrested for treason; the following day he is deported from the Soviet Union. In spring and summer, the first…
text: Aleksandr Isayevich Solzhenitsyn was a Soviet and Russian author and dissident who helped to raise global awareness of political repression in the Soviet Union, especially the Gulag prison system. He was awarded the 1970 Nobel Prize in Literature "for the ethical force with which he has pursued the indispensable traditions of Russian literature".

title: The first of Armistead Maupin's Tales of the City is published as a serial in The Pacific Sun (Marin County, California).
text: Armistead Jones Maupin Jr. is an American writer notable for Tales of the City, a series of novels set in San Francisco.

title: New Guildhall Library opens in the City of London.
text: The Guildhall Library is a public reference library in London, England, specialising in subjects relevant to London and its history. It is administered by the Corporation of London, the government of the City of London, which is the historical heart of London.

title: The Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics is founded by Allen Ginsberg and Anne Waldman.
text: The Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics is a school of Naropa University located in Boulder, Colorado, United States. It was founded in 1974 by Allen Ginsberg, Diane di Prima, and Anne Waldman, as part of Chögyam Trungpa Rinpoche's 100-year experiment and named after the Beat writer Jack Kerouac.

title: German writer Uwe Johnson moves to Sheerness on the English Isle of Sheppey.
text: Uwe Johnson was a German writer, editor, and scholar. Such prominent writers and scholars as Günter Grass and Hans Mayer declared Johnson to be the most significant writer to emerge from East Germany.
